newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - July 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - July 31.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian
press on July 31. Reuters has not verified these stories and
does not vouch for their accuracy.
State Secretary Murdiono said the government did not regard the sale of Indofood to a Singapore-based subsidairy of the Salim group as a case of capital flight.
The Palestinian ambassador to Indonesia shot a man in the foot in a Jakarta street after he thought the man was trying to rob him after his car had a flat tyre.
The U.S. under secretary of state for economic affairs, business and agriculture Stuart Eizenstat has commended Indonesia on its efforts to stabilise the rupiah.
Indonesia says South African president Nelson Mandela never discussed the freeing of East Timor rebel leader Xanana Gusmao during his recent state visit during which he met Gusmao in secret.
Candidates for the new national parliament elected last May, which takes office on October 1, will have their credentials checked again by the General Election Institute (LPU) and ABRI.
